rationale: Risperidone (D2/D3 + 5-HT2A + α1/α2 + H1; moderate anticholinergic activity) to amisulpride (selective D2/D3). Both drugs are high-potency D2 antagonists that elevate prolactin significantly. Common reasons: cost or formulary (amisulpride may be cheaper), desire for a drug without H1 antihistamine sedation, or negative symptom targeting at low doses (amisulpride 50–300 mg). Risperidone has less anticholinergic activity than olanzapine/quetiapine, so cross-taper can proceed at a moderate pace. Both drugs prolong QTc — ECG monitoring during the overlap period is important. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

schedule.notes: Start amisulpride 200 mg. Continue risperidone 4 mg. Baseline ECG (both drugs prolong QTc). Check renal function.
Increase amisulpride to 400 mg (target). Plateau risperidone. Monitor for additive QTc prolongation — check serum potassium if patient on diuretics or has risk factors.
Reduce risperidone to 2 mg. Amisulpride at target. Prolactin: additive elevation during overlap — if symptomatic (amenorrhoea, galactorrhoea), expedite risperidone withdrawal.
Reduce risperidone to 1 mg. Clinical stability maintained by amisulpride at therapeutic dose.
Stop risperidone. Continue amisulpride 400 mg. Repeat ECG at 4–6 weeks. Prolactin remains elevated on amisulpride — check if this was the reason for the switch.

doseRatios.equivalencyNote: Risperidone 4 mg ≈ amisulpride 400 mg (Leucht et al. CMD method, Schizophrenia Bulletin 2015). PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
